newsitem.title: USA: Two hurt in Maine commuter plane crash.
newsitem.headline: Two hurt in Maine commuter plane crash.

text.p: Two people were hurt when a USAir Express commuter plane bound for Boston crashed on the runway during takeoff at the Bangor International Airport Friday, officials said.

The cause of the accident involving a Beechcraft 1900 plane with 11 people on board was still under investigation, but weather conditions were poor and the runway was slippery, airport administrative assistant Connie Strout said.
Two people were taken to the Eastern Maine Medical Centre with "minor injuries," Strout added.

Initial reports said the aircraft had become airborne before hitting the runway, but airport director Robert Zeiglar said that had not been determined. Television pictures showed it on the runway with collapsed nosegear and a fractured fuselage.
Bangor International airport, a major refueling stop for transAtlantic freight and charter flights, remained closed because of the accident, Strout said.
Arlington, Virginia-based USAir did not immediately return phone calls seeking comment.
